## Teaching points

1. Microcytic anemia with low ferritin suggests iron deficiency. A stable patient also needs a plan to address the source of blood loss.
2. A stable hemoglobin of 9.6 g/dL is not by itself an indication for transfusion. Treat iron deficiency and investigate the bleeding source.
3. Hemoglobin recovery takes weeks, not an ED shift. Oral iron is discussed in the discharge plan because it is not an available catalog order.
